messages:
alex: heads-up — bumped micro-canary for route /v1/generate to 2% to test new kv-cache eviction heuristic. saw small tail-latency spike in the first 10m. anyone else observing?
maya-g: saw the same in prod-monitoring, +50ms p99 on a few p95 buckets. looks correlated with batch size changes.
sean: can you paste the routing config you used? was this header-based override or pure weight?
alex: weight only. new config: ```yaml
- match: path_prefix: /v1/generate
  canary:
    enabled: true
    traffic_percent: 2
    session_affinity: none
    fallback: route: stable
    override_headers: {}
```
priya: curious — did the canary hit a different quantized variant on the dedicated pool? that would explain latency.
alex: good point. we routed to model: gpt-neo-20q-8bit which is the quantized variant. stable is gpt-neo-20q-16bit.
jordan: if variant differs we should prefer header-annotated fallback so slow tails don't bleed. propose: add `x-model-variant` to telemetry and to console preview.
maya-g: agree. current console preview shows only weight and route match. UX asks for model variant + sample trace to be visible.
sean: also flagged: quota enforcement for canary is still global. a single tenant can push the canary over capacity and skew telemetry. need per-customer canary quota or throttling.
priya: per-tenant cap makes sense. suggestion: in routing policy allow `max_canary_concurrency_per_tenant` and drop to fallback when exceeded.
jordan: +1. and include a telemetry dimension `canary_over_cap` in the dashboard so we can filter out noisy signals.
alex: quick experiment: reverting canary to header-override flow instead of pure weight. header path: clients add `X-Canary: enable` for 2% of requests via splitter. less random noise. thoughts?
maya-g: that reduces sampling variance but requires client-side changes — for external customers that's non-starter. for internal jobs it's fine.
sean: we should also try adaptive ramping: if tail latency delta > 25ms for two consecutive 5m windows, auto-pause canary and route remaining traffic to fallback. makes rollouts safer.
priya: +auto-pause. But need console action button to resume with reason and TTL. ops will want manual override.
jordan: putting this together: 1) add `x-model-variant` to headers + traces, 2) add per-tenant canary concurrency quota, 3) implement auto-pause rule (25ms p99 delta over 10m) with console resume UX and audit log, 4) add telemetry flag `canary_paused_by_auto` to dashboard card.
alex: sounds good — can someone PR the routing schema change? small YAML/JSON bump to include new fields. I'll revert the live canary to 0.5% until we have rules.
maya-g: I'll open the dashboard card request and prototype the preview UI in the console.
sean: I'll work on the auto-pause controller and add an integration test. will add test for header + weight combo.
priya: I'll draft the quota knob and the policy semantics (drop vs fallback).
jordan: I'll add telemetry events and update the model-variant tagging in the runtime.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: infra/rollout-controller -> canary-autopause v0.3. ETA 18m :rocket:
